sections.h2: Where is Norwalk, Connecticut and how big is it?
sections.html:
Norwalk is a city in Fairfield County on the northern shore of Long Island Sound, part of the New York metropolitan area. It is the sixth most populous city in Connecticut, with 91,184 residents in 2020 and a 2024 estimate of 93,567.

The city covers about 36 square miles, but more than 13 square miles of that is water, including the Norwalk Islands and the harbor. Roger Ludlow bought the land east of the Norwalk River in 1640, and the town was incorporated in 1651. The Revolutionary War Battle of Norwalk burned most of the settlement, and the borough of Norwalk was created in 1836.

The 2020 census counted 38,152 housing units in the city, 5.4 percent of them vacant. About 29.6 percent of households were people living alone.

sections.h2: What are the six Norwalk taxing districts?
sections.html:
Norwalk has six taxing districts, and each one has its own property tax rate that reflects the services it receives from the city. This is the single most important fact for a Norwalk owner, because two houses a mile apart can carry different rates.

According to Wikipedia, the First, Second, Third and Sixth districts are political entities with their own elected officers, annual meetings and budgets. The Fourth and Fifth districts are not counted as separate governments and make up the city proper. The districts also supply utilities in parts of town:

  • The First Taxing District provides water to the Third, Fourth and Fifth districts.
  • The Second Taxing District serves sections of South Norwalk, East Norwalk, West Norwalk, Rowayton and Silvermine and operates South Norwalk Electric and Water.
  • The Third Taxing District provides electric power to East Norwalk.
  • Eversource supplies electricity and natural gas in most of the rest of the city.

Before you list, find out which district your address falls in and ask the Tax Collector whether the bill includes any district charge.

sections.h2: Who handles Norwalk property tax and land records?
sections.html:
Norwalk's Tax Assessor sets the assessment and the Tax Collector bills and collects the tax. Deeds and mortgage releases are filed with the Town Clerk, whose office is on the city website.

QuestionWhere it goes
How is my house assessed?Tax Assessor
What do I owe and when?Tax Collector
Where is my deed recorded?Town Clerk, Land Records
Town Clerk phone(203) 854-7745
Which district is my house in?Tax Collector or the city's tax district map

The Town Clerk's menu on norwalkct.gov lists Land Records and a Property Alert service. The Town Clerk page we did open gives the clerk's phone number and email.

sections.h2: What does the Norwalk economy look like?
sections.html:
Norwalk is a corporate address. Booking Holdings, Datto, FactSet, Pepperidge Farm, Terex and Xerox have headquarters here, according to Wikipedia, and the Financial Accounting Foundation and the Financial Accounting Standards Board are based in the city. Norwalk Hospital runs a 911 paramedic service that also covers New Canaan, Wilton, Weston and Westport.

Norwalk households report higher incomes than many Connecticut cities. The 2019 to 2023 Census survey figure on our page puts the median owner-occupied value at $535,000, and Wikipedia gives a household median income of $76,161 from an older survey. Whatever the home value, a written payoff from the Tax Collector is the starting point for any sale with taxes owed.

sections.h2: How do Norwalk neighborhoods differ for sellers?
sections.html:
Wikipedia lists dozens of Norwalk neighborhoods, from Rowayton and Silvermine to South Norwalk, Cranbury and Oak Hills. They differ by shoreline exposure, rail access and lot size.

  • Rowayton, East Norwalk and South Norwalk each have a Metro-North station.
  • Silvermine holds the city's highest point, 315 feet above sea level, on a golf course fairway.
  • Oak Hills Park in West Norwalk has a public golf course.
  • Manresa Island is the site of a closed power plant that began conversion to a park in 2025.

A lot near the water may need different insurance than one on higher ground. Ask a lender or insurer about the specific address.

sections.h2: How does Norwalk weather and coastline affect a house?
sections.html:
Norwalk gets about 48.5 inches of precipitation a year and about 28.6 inches of snow. Wikipedia records January highs near 37 degrees and July highs near 84. In 1955, three storms flooded Norwalk Harbor, and the city's topography is dominated by the coast, the Norwalk River and the islands.

For a seller, that points to roof, drainage, basement and gutter checks, plus an honest answer about any past water.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit shape Norwalk demand?
sections.html:
Interstate 95 and the Merritt Parkway run through the city, U.S. Route 1 follows local streets and Route 7 is an expressway through much of town. The Metro-North New Haven Line stops at Rowayton, South Norwalk and East Norwalk, and the Danbury Branch stops at Merritt 7. The Norwalk Transit District runs local buses that meet at a transportation hub.

Commuters to New York City value the rail stops, which can make a house near a station easier to market. Norwalk Public Schools operates the public schools, with Norwalk High School and Brien McMahon High School as the two largest high schools.

sections.h2: What state rules apply if you overpaid Norwalk property tax?
sections.html:
Connecticut law gives owners a window to claim a refund of an overpaid property tax. Under Section 12-129, a written application to the collector must be delivered or postmarked by the later of three years from the tax due date, any longer deadline the municipality sets by ordinance, or 90 days after a final court order or statutory process deletes an item of assessment.

The same section lets the municipality deny a refund when the same owner has another tax delinquency, and it applies the overpayment to that debt. The statute also bars refunds that rest on an error of judgment by the assessors. If you sold a house and think a Norwalk bill was paid twice at closing, send the collector a written request promptly, with your closing statement attached, and keep a copy.

sections.h2: What if you owe Norwalk property tax and need to sell?
sections.html: A Norwalk sale can pay off unpaid property tax from the proceeds. Request a written payoff from the Tax Collector, confirm your taxing district, check recorded liens with the Town Clerk and have an attorney review the closing figures. If repairs or tenant issues slow a traditional listing, an as-is cash sale is another route, and it is worth reading closely before you sign.

faqs.q: How many taxing districts does Norwalk have?
faqs.a: Six. Each has its own property tax rate that reflects the services it receives, and the Fourth and Fifth districts make up the city proper.

faqs.q: Who do I call for Norwalk land records?
faqs.a: The Norwalk Town Clerk, at (203) 854-7745, handles land records and recording.

faqs.q: Does Norwalk have its own utilities?
faqs.a: Parts of the city are served by taxing district utilities, including the Second Taxing District's South Norwalk Electric and Water and the Third District's East Norwalk electric service. Eversource covers most of the rest.
We could not confirm them on an opened official page, so check your bill or call the Tax Collector.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Norwalk house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff in writing first.
